messages:
ana: Heads up — during the last canary I noticed the dashboard's baseline is just a flat aggregate, which skews deltas when traffic split isn't 50/50. Can we show a weighted baseline that accounts for traffic split and routing rules? This is causing false positives on latency delta. cc @priya @chao
chao: Agreed. Current calc uses simple average across all traffic. Proposal: compute baseline as traffic-weighted mean of baseline variants for the same metric window and surface per-segment drilldowns. Math: baseline_weighted = sum(metric_i * weight_i) / sum(weights).
priya: +1 for weighted baseline. UX question: where do we show the split? Top banner or inline beside delta? I vote inline beside the delta with a hover explaining the weighting, plus a tiny sparkline for context.
matt: Note routing policies matter — header-based routing, QA pools, and reserved capacity buckets can create segments with zero/near-zero weight. Should either exclude segments with <1% traffic by default or surface them separately. Also proposing an API tweak: allow an optional query param 'segment_filter' on /rollouts/{id}/metrics to return only selected segments.
sara: For alerts: don't fire on weighted deltas unless both relative effect size and absolute change meet thresholds to avoid pager fatigue. Suggest defaults: effect_size > 5% AND absolute change (e.g., p50 latency) > 20ms OR traffic impact > X requests/sec. We could optionally include a p-value (permutation test) to reduce noise.
chao: Quick API/guard sketch — will iterate. Example guard config:
```json
{
  "guard_mode": "weighted",
  "weightedBaseline": true,
  "exclude_segments_below_pct": 1,
  "alert_condition": {
    "effect_size_pct": 5,
    "absolute_delta": 20,
    "min_traffic_change": 10
  },
  "explainability": {
    "include_bucket_counts": true,
    "tag_fields": ["routing.policy","split_key","split_value"]
  }
}
```
